questions.prompt: What happens when you breathe IN?
options: The diaphragm moves up and the ribs move down
The diaphragm moves down and the ribs move up and out
questions.explain: The chest space gets bigger, pressure drops and air rushes in.

questions.prompt: Complete the word equation for respiration in cells.
What is the difference between breathing and respiration?
options: Breathing moves air in and out of the lungs; respiration releases energy from food in every cell
Respiration happens only in the lungs
questions.explain: Breathing is a physical process; respiration is a chemical process.

questions.prompt: In the limewater test, exhaled air turned limewater milky much faster than room air. What does this show?
options: Exhaled air contains more carbon dioxide
questions.explain: CO₂ is a waste product of respiration.

questions.prompt: Adam took 16 breaths per minute at rest and 40 after running. By how many breaths per minute did his rate increase?
Plan an investigation into how exercise affects breathing rate.
questions.modelAnswer: Count breaths for one minute while sitting quietly (repeat three times and average). Then do a fixed exercise, such as 30 jumping jacks, and immediately count breaths for one minute. Repeat for different amounts of exercise (e.g. 10, 20, 30 jumping jacks), resting until breathing returns to normal between tests. Keep the same person, the same type of exercise and the same counting method. Present results in a table and bar chart.
rubric: Independent variable: amount or type of exercise
questions.explain: Criterion B: plan a safe, fair test.

questions.prompt: Order the path of air when you breathe in.
questions.explain: Oxygen diffuses from the air sacs into the blood.

questions.prompt: During very hard exercise, muscles may get cramps from a build-up of…
questions.explain: When there isn't enough oxygen, muscles respire anaerobically and make lactic acid.
